# idna-rs — Rust port of `idna-cpp/tests/test4.cpp`

A zero-dependency (std-only) Rust 2021 reimplementation of the four `idna`
domain predicates exercised by `test4.cpp`, byte-for-byte compatible with the
reference C++ binary.

## Layout

```
/output
├── Cargo.toml          # no [dependencies]
├── test4.rs            # entry point (package root, per spec)
├── src/
│   ├── lib.rs          # library root
│   └── idna/
│       ├── mod.rs      # public API re-exports
│       ├── limits.rs   # MAX_LABEL_LEN / MAX_DOMAIN_LEN
│       ├── validate.rs # is_valid_domain, is_valid_label
│       ├── ascii.rs    # is_ascii_domain, is_idn_domain
│       └── cli.rs      # argv handling + output formatting
└── tests/spec.rs       # table-driven test over verified reference outputs
```

## Building

```sh
cargo build --release          # -> target/release/test4
rustc -O test4.rs -o test4     # standalone; also works with --edition 2021
```

`test4.rs` pulls the library modules in with `#[path]` rather than as an extern
crate, so a bare `rustc test4.rs` works. All paths in `mod.rs` are `self::`
qualified so the standalone build succeeds under edition 2015 (what bare
`rustc` defaults to) as well as under 2021.

## Reverse-engineered specification

`idna.hpp` is not present in the dataset, so behaviour was derived purely by
probing `dataset/test4_executable`.

### CLI contract

`argv[1]` is the domain to test, defaulting to `example.com` when absent
(matching `if (argc > 1) input = argv[1];`). Extra arguments are ignored. An
explicitly empty `argv[1]` is honoured and does *not* fall back to the default.
Exit code is always 0.

### Output

Four lines, each a single `1` or `0` followed by `\n` — `is_valid_domain`,
`is_valid_label`, `is_ascii_domain`, `is_idn_domain`. `std::cout << bool` uses
numeric formatting, so never `true`/`false`. A run emits exactly 8 bytes.

### Predicates

All four are decided on **bytes**, never on Unicode scalar values:

| predicate          | semantics                        |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------- |
| `is_valid_domain`  | `1 <= len <= 255` bytes          |
| `is_valid_label`   | `1 <= len <= 63` bytes           |
| `is_ascii_domain`  | every byte `<= 0x7F` (empty: 1)  |
| `is_idn_domain`    | any byte `> 0x7F` (empty: 0)     |

Three findings are worth calling out, because a "reasonable" implementation
gets each of them wrong:

**1. The validity predicates ignore content entirely.** They are pure length
checks. A sweep of every byte value `0x01..=0xFF`, alone and embedded as
`a<BYTE>b.com`, found nothing either predicate rejects. `"."`, `".."`,
`"a..b"`, `"-a.com"`, `"a b.com"`, `"*.com"` and 255 consecutive dots are all
"valid". There is no empty-label check, no hyphen-position check, no character
allow-list, and no per-label length check inside `is_valid_domain` — a 64-byte
label inside a short name still yields a valid domain.

**2. The limits count bytes, not code points.** 21×`"例"` is 63 bytes / 21 code
points and is a valid label; 63×`"例"` is 189 bytes / 63 code points and is
not. So `.len()` is correct and `.chars().count()` is not.

**3. The domain limit is 255, not the RFC-1035 presentation limit of 253.** A
255-byte name is accepted, 256 is rejected. No trailing dot is stripped first,
so `"a"×255 + "."` is 256 bytes and therefore invalid.

Also note `is_idn_domain` does not look at the `xn--` ACE prefix:
`"xn--fsq.com"` is reported as ASCII and *not* as an IDN. No normalisation,
case folding, or punycode conversion happens anywhere.

## The `args()` vs `args_os()` deviation

`cli.rs` reads arguments with `std::env::args_os()` rather than
`std::env::args()`. This is deliberate and load-bearing: `std::env::args()`
**panics** on an argument that is not valid UTF-8, whereas the C++ binary
accepts one happily —

```
$ dataset/test4_executable $'\xff'
1
1
0
1
```

`std::string` carries no encoding guarantee, so the reference implementation is
operating on bytes. Staying in the byte domain is what actually reproduces it;
using `args()` would abort with a panic on inputs the reference handles. Both
are `std::env` argument accessors, so no arg-parsing crate is involved either
way.

## Verification

`tests/spec.rs` asserts the reference outputs for the documented examples plus
every boundary and edge case above. Beyond that, the port was diffed against
`dataset/test4_executable` over several thousand inputs — the full `0x01..=0xFF`
byte sweep alone and embedded, every length from 0 to 300 in ASCII and in 2-,
3- and 4-byte UTF-8, invalid UTF-8 (lone continuation bytes, truncated and
overlong sequences), randomised strings, and the CLI matrix (no args, empty
arg, extra args, flag-like args) — comparing `od -c` of stdout plus exit codes,
with zero mismatches.
